hono-5110:
`methodOverride` in query mode crashes when the request has a body

Using `methodOverride` with the `query` option works for body-less requests, but as soon as the original request carries a body the override fails on Node (undici). The request never reaches the overridden handler and the app responds with a 500; the underlying error is

```
TypeError: RequestInit: duplex option is required when sending a body.
```

Repro:

```ts
import { Hono } from 'hono'
import { methodOverride } from 'hono/method-override'

const app = new Hono()
app.use('/posts/*', methodOverride({ app, query: '_method' }))
app.on(['post', 'delete'], '/posts', async (c) =>
  c.json({
    method: c.req.method,
    body: await c.req.text(),
    queryValue: c.req.query('_method') ?? null,
  })
)

const res = await app.request('/posts?_method=delete', {
  method: 'POST',
  body: new URLSearchParams({ message: 'Hello' }),
})
console.log(res.status) // 500
```

Expected: `200` with

```json
{ "method": "DELETE", "body": "message=Hello", "queryValue": null }
```

i.e. the request is re-dispatched as `DELETE`, the original body is forwarded untouched, and the `_method` query parameter is stripped from the forwarded URL. Requests without a body (and the existing rule that `GET` is never overridden) should keep working as they do today.

hono-4998:
IPv6 unspecified address `::` is rendered as `:`

The IPv6 helpers used by the `ipRestriction` middleware produce an invalid string for the all-zero address. `convertIPv6BinaryToString(0n)` returns `":"` instead of the canonical `"::"` (RFC 5952).

```ts
convertIPv6BinaryToString(0n)                        // ":"  (expected "::")
convertIPv6BinaryToString(convertIPv6ToBinary('::')) // ":"  (expected "::")
convertIPv6ToBinary(convertIPv6BinaryToString(0n))   // throws "Invalid IPv6 address: :"
```

`":"` is not a valid IPv6 address (`net.isIP(':') === 0`), and it doesn't round-trip back through `convertIPv6ToBinary`. Anything that normalizes addresses through these helpers can end up with the bogus `":"`. One example is an `ipRestriction` rule list that contains `'::'`.

Other addresses, including the IPv4-mapped form (`::ffff:1.2.3.4`), are already rendered correctly.

Expected:

- `convertIPv6BinaryToString(0n) === '::'`
- `convertIPv6BinaryToString(convertIPv6ToBinary('::')) === '::'`
- `convertIPv6ToBinary(convertIPv6BinaryToString(0n)) === 0n`

The output for every other address should stay as it is now.
hono-5096:
`hc`: path params break when one param name is a prefix of another

With the RPC client, a route whose params share a prefix (e.g. `:idType` and `:id`) gets a mangled URL:

```ts
// server: app.get('/:idType/:id', ...)
client[':idType'][':id'].$url({ param: { id: '1', idType: '2' } })
// expected: http://localhost/2/1
// actual:   http://localhost/1Type/:id
```

The value meant for `:id` gets written into the middle of the `:idType` segment, and `:id` itself is left unreplaced. The result also depends on the key order of the `param` object: with `{ idType: '2', id: '1' }` it happens to work.

The problem is in the client's shared path-template substitution step, i.e. the utility that takes a URL template like `http://localhost/:idType/:id` plus a params record and returns the filled-in URL. `$url`, `$get`, `$ws` and the rest all go through it. That step on its own should return `http://localhost/2/1` for `{ id: '1', idType: '2' }`, whatever the key order. Reordering keys inside `hc` is not enough.

Expected: a `:name` placeholder only matches a whole param token, meaning one that ends at a `/` or at the end of the URL. The existing forms must keep working: `:name{regex}` constraints, and optional `:name?` params (an optional param with no value is dropped together with its slash).
hono-5138:
`writeSSE()` can't send an empty `id` to reset Last-Event-ID

Per the HTML spec for server-sent events, an `id:` field with an empty value resets the client's last event ID, so after a reconnect the browser no longer sends a `Last-Event-ID` header. There's currently no way to do that with `streamSSE`: passing `id: ''` to `writeSSE()` drops the field entirely.

```ts
import { streamSSE } from 'hono/streaming'

app.get('/sse', (c) =>
  streamSSE(c, async (stream) => {
    await stream.writeSSE({ data: 'reset', id: '' })
  })
)
```

Actual body: `'data: reset\n\n'`

Expected body: exactly `'data: reset\nid: \n\n'`

Only an omitted `id` (`undefined`) should mean "no id field". An empty string is meaningful and should be written out as `id: ` with nothing after it. The other fields should behave as they do now: `retry: 0` is still emitted, `event` is still left out when not given, and the existing CR/LF validation of `event`/`id` should keep throwing.

Spec: https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/server-sent-events.html#the-last-event-id-header
hono-5255:
`accepts()` ignores `type/*` wildcards in the Accept header

With the default matching (no custom `match` option), `accepts()` from `hono/accepts` only matches Accept entries that are exactly equal to one of the `supports` values. A client that sends a subtype wildcard like `application/*` gets the `default` even though the server supports an `application/...` type.

```ts
import { accepts } from 'hono/accepts'

// Accept: application/*
accepts(c, {
  header: 'Accept',
  supports: ['application/json', 'text/html'],
  default: 'text/html',
})
// actual: 'text/html'   expected: 'application/json'
```

Expected behaviour for the default matcher:

- `type/*` matches any supported value with the same main type. The result is the matching entry from `supports` (the first one, in `supports` order), never the wildcard string itself.
- Entries are still tried in order of `q`. At equal `q`, an exact type is preferred over a `type/*` wildcard.
- The global wildcards `*/*` and `*` do **not** match anything. They fall through, and if nothing else matches, the `default` is returned. So:
  - `Accept: text/plain, */*;q=0.5` with `supports: ['application/json']`, `default: 'text/html'` gives `'text/html'`
  - `Accept-Encoding: *` with `supports: ['gzip', 'deflate']`, `default: 'identity'` gives `'identity'`
  - `Accept: */*, text/*` with `supports: ['application/json', 'text/plain']`, `default: 'application/json'` gives `'text/plain'`
  - `Accept: */*, application/json` with `supports: ['text/html', 'application/json']` gives `'application/json'`

Exact matches and custom `match` functions should behave exactly as they do today.
hono-5272:
`hc`: an `undefined` entry in a query array is sent as `"undefined"`

The RPC client already skips a query value that is `undefined` at the top level, but it doesn't skip `undefined` entries inside an array. They get stringified and go out on the wire as the literal string `"undefined"`.

No cast is needed to hit this. A validator whose query field is an optional union gives the client an input type of `(string | undefined)[] | undefined`:

```ts
const app = new Hono().get(
  '/search',
  validator('query', () => ({}) as { tag: (string | undefined)[] | undefined }),
  (c) => c.json({ ok: true })
)
const client = hc<typeof app>('http://localhost')

await client.search.$get({ query: { tag: ['a', undefined, 'b'] } })
// actual:   GET http://localhost/search?tag=a&tag=undefined&tag=b
// expected: GET http://localhost/search?tag=a&tag=b
```

The fix belongs in the default query serializer, i.e. the `buildSearchParams` that `hc` uses when you don't pass your own `buildSearchParams` option. Called directly, that default serializer should give:

- `{ tag: ['a', undefined, 'b'] }` gives `tag=a&tag=b`
- `{ tag: [undefined, undefined] }` gives `''` (the key disappears entirely)
- `{ tag: ['a', '', 'b'] }` gives `tag=a&tag=&tag=b`. Empty strings are real values and must still be sent.

Out of scope: `null` keeps its current behaviour (serialized as `"null"`, the same as at the top level), and the `form` body path is a separate issue.
hono-5349:
Accept parsing ignores an uppercase `Q=` weight

RFC 9110 §12.4.2 says the name of the `q` weight parameter is case-insensitive, but `parseAccept` (from `hono/utils/accept`) only recognises lowercase `q`. A header that spells it `Q=` is treated as if it had no weight:

```ts
parseAccept('text/html;Q=0.5')
// actual:   [{ type: 'text/html', params: { Q: '0.5' }, q: 1 }]
// expected: [{ type: 'text/html', params: { Q: '0.5' }, q: 0.5 }]

parseAccept('text/html;Q=0')[0].q
// actual: 1, expected: 0

parseAccept('text/html;Q=0.5,application/json;q=0.9').map((x) => x.type)
// actual:   ['text/html', 'application/json']
// expected: ['application/json', 'text/html']
```

This matters anywhere a weight decides something:

- `accepts()` can pick the entry the client ranked lower.
- `compress` reads `Accept-Encoding: gzip;Q=0` as "gzip preferred" instead of "gzip not acceptable".
- `languageDetector` gets the wrong language ordering.

Expected: an uppercase `Q` gives the same `q` value and the same sort order as lowercase `q`. `params` should keep the parameter name exactly as it was sent (`{ Q: '0.5' }`), because it's observable through the `Accept` type and through custom `match` functions. Existing quality handling must not change: a missing `q` still means `1`, and a lowercase `q=invalid` still keeps `params.q === 'invalid'` with `q: 1`.
hono-5379:
JWT `verify()` throws a raw `DOMException` for a non-base64url signature

If the third (signature) part of a token contains characters outside the base64url alphabet, `verify()` (from `hono/jwt`, also `Jwt.verify` from `hono/utils/jwt`) rejects with a platform `InvalidCharacterError` `DOMException` instead of one of Hono's JWT error types:

```ts
import { verify } from 'hono/jwt'

const tok =
  'eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJtZXNzYWdlIjoiaGVsbG8gd29ybGQifQ.@@@@'

await verify(tok, 'a-secret', 'HS256')
// rejects with a DOMException (InvalidCharacterError), not a JwtTokenInvalid
```

A malformed header or payload already produces `JwtTokenInvalid`, so the signature part is the odd one out. Code that branches on `err instanceof JwtTokenInvalid` misses this case. `verifyWithJwks()` inherits the same behaviour. (The `jwt` middleware turns any error into a 401, so it isn't visibly affected.)

Expected:

- The token above rejects with `JwtTokenInvalid`, with message `invalid JWT token: <token>`, the same as for a malformed header/payload.
- An **empty** signature part (`header.payload.`) still rejects with `JwtTokenSignatureMismatched` (`token(<token>) signature mismatched`), as it does today.
- A well-formed but wrong signature is still `JwtTokenSignatureMismatched`. Errors coming from the crypto layer itself should not be converted into `JwtTokenInvalid`.
